title: Nanomotion technology: an innovative method to study cell metabolism in Escherichia coli, as a potential indicator for tolerance.
authors: Aubry, Christele; Kebbi-Beghdadi, Carole; Luraschi-Eggemann, Amanda; Cathomen, Gino; Cichocka, Danuta; Sturm, Alexander; Greub, Gilbert; The Eradiamr Consortium
one_liner_zh: 该文利用纳米运动技术结合机器学习研究大肠杆菌代谢与抗生素耐受性，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Introduction. Antibiotic tolerance corresponds to the bacterial ability to survive a transient exposure to antibiotics and is often associated with treatment failure. Current methods of identifying tolerance based on bacterial growth are time-consuming. This study explores the use of a growth-independent method utilizing nanomotion technology to detect antibiotic-tolerant bacteria.Hypothesis. The nanomotion signal obtained from a nanomechanical sensor measures real-time metabolic activity and cellular processes and could provide valuable information about the tolerance of bacteria to antibiotics that cannot be detected by standard antibiotic susceptibility tests.Aim. The aim of this study is to investigate the potential of nanomotion technology to record antibiotic-tolerant bacteria.Methodology. We generated a slow-growing Escherichia coli strain by manipulating mazF expression levels and confirmed its viability by several standard methods. We subsequently measured its nanomotion and the nanomotion of the WT E. coli in the presence or absence of antibiotics. Supervised machine learning was employed to distinguish slow-growing from exponentially growing bacteria. Observations for bacterial nanomotions were confirmed by standard kill curves.Results. We distinguished slow-growing from exponentially growing bacteria using specific features from the nanomotion signal. Furthermore, the exposition of both growth phenotypes to polymyxin decreased the nanomotion signal indicating cell death. Similarly, when exponentially growing cells were exposed to ampicillin, an antibiotic whose efficacy depends on the growth rate, the nanomotion signal also decreased. In contrast, the nanomotion signal remained unchanged for slow-growing bacteria upon exposure to ampicillin. In addition, antibiotic exposure can cause bacterial elongation, in which the biomass of a cell increases without cell division. By overexpressing sulA, we mimicked antibiotic-induced elongation. Differences in the nanomotion signal were observed when comparing elongating and non-elongating phenotypes.Conclusion. This work shows that nanomotion signals entail information about the reaction to antibiotics that standard MIC-based antibiotic susceptibility tests cannot detect. In the future, nanomotion-based antibiotic tolerance tests could be developed for clinical use in chronic or relapsing infections.
abstract_zh: 引言。抗生素耐受性（antibiotic tolerance）是指细菌在短暂暴露于抗生素后存活的能力，常与治疗失败相关。目前基于细菌生长的耐受性鉴定方法耗时较长。本研究探讨利用基于纳米运动技术（nanomotion technology）的非生长依赖方法来检测抗生素耐受性细菌。假设。纳米机械传感器获得的纳米运动信号可实时测量代谢活性和细胞过程，可能提供关于细菌对抗生素耐受性的有价值信息，而这些信息无法通过标准抗生素敏感性测试检测到。目的。本研究旨在探讨纳米运动技术在记录抗生素耐受性细菌方面的潜力。方法。我们通过调控mazF表达水平构建了一株生长缓慢的大肠杆菌（Escherichia coli）菌株，并通过多种标准方法确认其活性。随后，在有无抗生素条件下，测量了该菌株及野生型（WT）大肠杆菌的纳米运动。采用监督机器学习区分缓慢生长与指数生长的细菌。细菌纳米运动的观察结果通过标准杀菌曲线进行验证。结果。我们利用纳米运动信号的特定特征区分了缓慢生长与指数生长的细菌。此外，将两种生长表型暴露于多粘菌素（polymyxin）后，纳米运动信号下降，表明细胞死亡。同样，当指数生长的细胞暴露于氨苄青霉素（ampicillin）——一种其效力依赖于生长速率的抗生素——时，纳米运动信号也下降。相反，缓慢生长的细菌在暴露于氨苄青霉素后，纳米运动信号保持不变。此外，抗生素暴露可导致细菌伸长，即细胞生物量增加而不发生分裂。通过过表达sulA，我们模拟了抗生素诱导的伸长。比较伸长与非伸长表型时，观察到纳米运动信号的差异。结论。本研究表明，纳米运动信号包含关于抗生素反应的信息，而这些信息是标准基于最低抑菌浓度（MIC）的抗生素敏感性测试无法检测到的。未来，基于纳米运动的抗生素耐受性测试可开发用于慢性或复发性感染的临床诊断。
